chapter_theme: General songs (பொதுப்பாடல்கள், 4 of 21): pleas against disease, birth and the decaying body, against flattering patrons and courtesans, and above all for the inner way (silence as temple, breath and the six centres, the self lost so that all becomes one, the abode of supreme wisdom that no fire, wind or weapon touches), set to praise that calls Murugan the Meru of compassion.
structure_note: Two rhythm groups. 1038 to 1042 run in long syllables (தானா) and share the refrain சேயே வேளே பூவே கோவே தேவே தேவப் பெருமாளே; 1043 to 1051 run in a Sanskrit-heavy metre ending கருணை மேருவே தேவர் பெருமாளே. The yogic and non-dual songs (1043 to 1045, 1047, 1049, 1050) are the chapter's core; 1046 and 1051 confess women, 1041 and 1048 the funeral and Death's messengers.

1037.reading: The poet asks that wind-disease, headache, colic and swollen belly not come near, that he not enter the womb-path again in this body packed with illusion, nor whirl in births like waves beating on the sea, and asks whether he will gain Murugan's paired anklets so that the many devotees who recite may also reach the goal. The praise calls Murugan kin to those who sing the Vedas with music so that their ruin perishes, the hero whose feet Vishnu and Brahma seek, and the Lord whose vel powdered Sura.
1037.nuance: The plea names diseases one by one (வாதம், தலைவலி, சூலம், பெருவயிறு), the body's own failings before birth's cycle. ஓதும் பல அடியாரும் கதி பெற யான் உன் கழலிணை பெறுவேனோ seems to ask the feet not only for himself but so that other devotees reach the goal, though the clause could also mean 'as many devotees have'.

1038.reading: The poet asks whether he, a dog, must die without being saved, not tending the swinging hut of flesh with its ceaseless disease, his mind apart from worldly custom, unreached by the liberation in which 'I am you and you are I' that the many Vedas' meanings cannot search out. The praise calls Murugan sky, wind, fire, water and earth and their owner, life of the doe-like Valli, bearer of the cock banner, the honey of the hill where honey falls in long forest streams.
1038.nuance: நானே நீயாய் நீயே நானாய் is the non-dual goal stated in four words; the Vedas' meanings cannot seek it (நாடா வீடு). The praise reuses the five-element formula of Murugan as everything and its owner. The rhythm of long syllables makes several splits uncertain, and ஡ in the second line stands for ஊ (ஊசாடு ஊசல் குடில).

1039.reading: The poet seems to recite the flattery poets give patrons: 'you are like the deathless, ageless Kama, a giver who pours grace, a knower and king, life to those who depend on you, like Mal with his arrow, like the rain cloud', and asks whether he must go in vain to such people who neither fit the praise nor sing. The praise names Siva, lord who rides the bull, whose feet in the depth of the netherworld Vishnu lying on the serpent in the ocean could not find, and calls Murugan his treasure, wearing the vetchi garland.
1039.nuance: The opening string of comparisons (வேளே போல்வாய், தாதாவே, மாலே போல்வாய், காரே போல்வாய்) is the stock language of praise-poems to patrons, and யான் வீணே ஏகத்திடலாமோ regrets carrying it to unworthy men; the same complaint returns in 1062. The rhythm hides word breaks, so whether the comparisons are the poet's flattery or addressed to Murugan is not certain.

1040.reading: Before the hut of many doors made of sinew, skin and water becomes a place for dogs and ghouls to crowd round, the poet asks Murugan of the twelve garlanded shoulders, life of the gods who take refuge, to give him, a dog, without delay the strength to sing his feet with his tongue. The praise names Vishnu who rules the seven worlds with one step and Brahma of the Vedas, who could not reach the feet through earth and sky, and Siva of the golden hair who rides the bull and lives with his lady.
1040.nuance: நானா வாசல் குடில், the hut of many doors, is the body with its openings, food for dogs and ghouls once dead. Two lines of the praise (பர்ழு டேவா னூடே பர்ரு டேயூர்) are garbled; the sense of Vishnu and Brahma searching the feet through earth and sky is a guess from what survives.

1041.reading: The poet pictures mother, uncles, women and cousins turned to strangers throwing this hut of illusion and infatuation into the long fire, then going down to bathe in the water, and asks Murugan, whose form is knowledge, to look on him and give grace at his flower feet before life leaves in that anguish. The praise names the vel that relieved the gods' fear and Siva who destroyed the wicked, whose son Murugan is.
1041.nuance: மாறானார் போல் neatly says the kin act as if they were strangers once the body is ash. போதாகாரா, 'whose form is knowledge', is the address of the plea. A line of the praise (தீயு ஧ட்முள்) is corrupt.

1042.reading: The poet asks Murugan to rule him by saying, as a teacher: 'Come, fool, listen: do not play in the filth of desire and infatuation for women; look within; the unchanging flame of wisdom stands, find it without searching; see the endless meaning of the Vedas that is the true gain', for who else on earth is fit to rule him. The praise calls Murugan the commander of the gods' army, whose twelve shoulders embrace the millet-field girl, and whose arrow, sword and vel cut Sura to dust.
1042.nuance: The plea is cast as the guru's own words the poet wants to hear, beginning வாராய் பேதாய் கேளாய். ஆராயாதே ஆராய், 'investigate without investigating', points to knowledge not won by effort. The word splits are often doubtful in this rhythm.

1043.reading: The poet asks whether, taking as his temple the silence that no one can measure in breadth or length, strewing flowers of the joy of great knowledge on the seat of ritual, he will perform the great worship of the Siva-form beyond all Vedas, all words, all action, all disciplines and all residual impressions. The praise is a run of Sanskrit epithets for Murugan of the peacock and the vel, pure and all-pervading, delight of poets, ending in the Meru of compassion.
1043.nuance: அரிய மோனமே கோயில்: the temple is silence, and the worship is inward, offered to what is beyond Vedas, words, actions and vasanas (சகல வேதனாதீத, சகல வாசகாதீத, சகல வாசனாதீத). The praise packs Sanskrit compounds whose splits are hard to fix.

1044.reading: The poet asks not to become a graceless karma-yogi of improper conduct who, thinking that the breath that leaves daily without pause will give liberation if turned back, stumbles endlessly on earth, but to be given Murugan's lotus feet so that, shaking off body, self and the instruments as separate things and melting into the feet beyond words, he may become a supreme yogi of noble conduct. The praise tells of the churning of the ocean with Meru, the serpent and the moon pained, by Gopala, whose nephew Murugan is, and of Siva with trident and skull, whose son he is.
1044.nuance: The song distinguishes two yogis: one who relies on stopping the breath (வாயு அடைய மீளில் வீடாகும் என நாடி) but lacks grace, and the one who melts into the feet. உடலம் வேறு யான் வேறு கரணம் வேறு: body, self and faculties are seen apart and shaken off. In the praise வா஡ணச is corrupt, perhaps for வாரீச, the sea-born Lakshmi.

1045.reading: The poet asks for the state beyond the heart's imagining in which 'mine' and 'I' fall away and everyone and everything becomes himself, reached as the pure breath stops, the fire is kindled at the root above the lotus navel and the nectar drunk, step by step without wavering, striking Yama and gaining the power to travel the sky. The praise compares Murugan's peacock racing over the spheres to Vishnu stretching over the seven worlds, and calls him cloud, ocean and Meru of compassion.
1045.nuance: The yogic steps (breath held, fire at மூலம், nectar drunk, ascent by சோபானம், a ladder) and their powers (எமனை மோதி, ஆகாச கமனம்) lead to the stated goal: எனது யானும் வேறாகி எவரும் யாதும் யானாகும், loss of ego and identity with all. A line near the start is corrupt (பான ஧ம்முல), and the river names in the praise are unclear.

1046.reading: The poet describes women whose blue eyes, sharper than arrow and vel, maddening like intoxicating drink, long and reaching to the ears, make even sleepless gods and Vedic ascetics free of infatuation resolve to ride the palm-stem horse, and asks Murugan to show a path by which he, drooping with such women, may be saved. The praise is a hymn to Uma, daughter of the Himalaya, Abhirami, Syamala, supreme yogini, Mahamayi, half of the lord of Kailasa, and calls Murugan the poet of Vedic songs fragrant with the nectar of her breast.
1046.nuance: மடலேற, mounting the palm-stem horse, is the akam lover's public declaration of desperate love; here even ascetics are driven to it by the women's eyes. கனதனாசல அமுதூறல் கமழும் ஆரணா கீத கவிதை வாண points to Sambandar, fed by Uma's milk and singing the hymns, identified with Murugan.

1047.reading: Having described drinking a woman's mouth until thirst goes, sinking in the sea of pleasure with a heart that melts and does not stray, the poet asks what Murugan's form is: the sum of Veda, chariyai, yoga, kriyai and gnanam, the world with form beginning with the elements, the bud of the six supports, the support-less, or the formless. The praise calls Murugan guru to Siva, who wears on his head the lotus feet of the chaste hunter girl, and who circled the seven worlds when the elephant-faced god on his mouse circled their father.
1047.nuance: The two halves of the plea are joined by the word வடிவேயோ, and it is unclear whether the poet asks what Murugan's form is or contrasts the lovers' oneness with it. சடாதார முகுளம், the bud of the six centres, and நிராதாரம், the support-less, name yogic levels. The last line alludes to the contest in which Ganapati circled his parents and Murugan circled the world.

1048.reading: Before Death, sent by Yama to break the life in the hut of blood and skin, comes with his cruel noose and trident and his diseases, the poet asks Murugan, whose vel freed sun, moon, gods and the milk ocean from fear, to grant him grace to sing his feet with love. The praise names Krishna who felled the marutha trees and played the flute, who ran when the elephant cried 'Root!', husband of the cowherd women and Rama obedient to his mother's word, whose nephew Murugan is, and Siva the skull-bearer who dances with ghosts, whose son he is.
1048.nuance: காலன் is here Yama's servant (ஏமனால் ஏவி விடு காலன்), coming with பாசம், சூலம் and diseases as weapons. பழுது றா பாவாணர் எழுதொணாத தோள்: the shoulders flawless poets cannot write, the praise admitting its limit.

1049.reading: The poet asks Murugan to tell him where the abode of supreme wisdom is: unheard through scripture, unseen by those of ritual conduct, not reached above turiya, followed by no one, untouched by great maya, unending bliss that does not die in fire, wither in the sun, burn in the undersea fire, fall in the wind, sink in the ocean or perish when weapons strike. The praise calls Murugan the vel-thrower on the snowy peak, teacher whom Brahma and Vishnu esteem, and treasure of Siva of the golden bow who moves in sky and earth and dances in Kailasa.
1049.nuance: The list of negations (fire, sun, wind, ocean, weapons) recalls the Gita's description of the self that weapons do not cut nor fire burn, though the text does not name it; here it describes the abode of wisdom. துரிய மீது சாராது: even turiya, the fourth state, does not reach it. The question பரம ஞான வீடு ஏது புகல்வாயே recurs in 1054.

1050.reading: The poet asks whether Murugan, who cannot be touched or seen directly or answered by those who recite scripture, who is lord of the directions, the one turiya, other than all and knowledge itself, and who entered the body of long arms and legs saying 'you and I', will not tell him the one truth by which he may go before the fierce messenger sent by Death arrives. The praise names the vel that killed crores of Suras, the guardian of the girl born of a doe, and Siva the poison-throated dancer riding the bull.
1050.nuance: நீ நானும் என நேர்மை நூல் கூறி: the Lord entering the body and teaching 'you and I' may point to the non-dual teaching of 1038. மான் ஈனும் அரிவை is Valli, born of a doe. The plea's last clause is hard to split, and the line has a stray ** in the source.

1051.reading: The poet describes lovemaking in moonlight as Kama's wind blows, in garden shade and on the mansion's upper floor, on a fragrant bed, drinking the honey of lips like silk-cotton flowers and pressing breasts to his chest, and vows that even as infatuation grows he will not forget Murugan's kadamba-garlanded feet. The praise shows the child Kumara climbing onto Siva's matted crown with Ganga and the serpent, never parting from the hunter girl, and the vel that turned Sura's army to dust, consort of the elephant's girl.
1051.nuance: Unusually, the plea does not ask to be freed from women: மால் கூரினும் உன் நீப சீர்பாதம் மறவேனே, even in growing infatuation he will not forget the feet. The child climbing the father's matted crown (சடில மோலி மீது ஏறு குமர) is a tender image. ஡ stands for ஊ (ஊதை, ஊறு), and பி஧ல்முழ்க is corrupt for பில் மூழ்க.

links.note: Both follow the funeral to its end: the kin burn the body and then bathe in the water (நீரினில் மூழ்கி; போதா நீருடே போய் மூழ்கா). The Tirumanthiram adds that they stop thinking of the dead; 1041 says they act as strangers.

The Tirumanthiram teaches that if the breath stays still with the mind there is no birth or death; 1044 rejects the yogi who thinks turning back the breath gives liberation but lacks grace, and asks instead for the feet. The point of difference depends on reading 1044 as faulting yoga without grace, not breath control as such.

The song asks that the poet not enter the womb's path again (வாழுங் கருவழி மருவாதே) and asks for Murugan's paired anklets (உன் கழலிணை பெறுவேனோ). Tirumanthiram 1597 reports the result: the guru set his feet on the poet's head (திருவடி வைத்தென் சிரத்து) so that the womb's path drained away (கருவழி வாற்றிட). The same word கருவழி ties the plea to the Tirumanthiram's account of the feet ending it.

The song names the liberation it has not reached as 'I become you and you become I' (நானே நீயாய் நீயே நானாய்), which the Vedas' meanings cannot search out. Tirumanthiram 1788 states the same goal as experience: on nearing him there is no separate 'I' or 'you' (நானென நீயென வேறில்லை), as flesh and the life in it stand together. Both make the end of the I-you division the mark of release.

The song uses the words நானே நீயாய் நீயே நானாய் for non-dual liberation. In song 626 the same formula is the courtesans' shameless oath, நீயே நானே என்றொரு சத்தியம், sworn to any man for money. The poet uses one phrase for the highest union and for the falsest, which shows how he sets bought love against union with the Lord.

The song repeats the stock comparisons poets give patrons (வேளே போல்வாய், மாலே போல்வாய், காரே போல்வாய்) and regrets carrying them in vain (வீணே) to men who neither fit the praise nor give. Naladiyar 219 judges abuse better than praise of qualities a man does not have (இல்ல புகழ்தலின் வைதலே நன்று). The Naladiyar gives the moral rule; the song confesses breaking it.

This song regrets praise wasted on patrons in the stock comparisons of patronage poetry (வேளே போல்வாய் ... காரே போல்வாய்). Song 1062 makes the same confession about love poetry, the 'is it sword, vel, carp or deer?' questions (வாளோ வேலோ சேலோ மானோ) sung to courtesans, ending கவி பாடா நாயேன். Together they show the poet treating his own craft, spent on patrons or on women, as the thing to repent.

Naladiyar 26 says that once the dancer has left the skin bag (தோற்பை), it does not matter what is done with the body. The song takes the body's end, the hut of sinew, skin and water (நாரால் தோல் நீரால்) becoming a place for dogs and ghouls, as a deadline and asks for the strength to sing the feet before then (நாய்பேய் சூழ்கைக்கு இடமாமுன் ... தாள் பாடு ஆண்மைத் திறல் தாராய்). The Naladiyar's indifference to the corpse becomes in the song a reason to act while the body still serves.

This song asks Murugan to rule him by speaking as teacher, scripting the words he wants to hear (வாராய் பேதாய் கேளாய்) that point to the unchanging flame of wisdom. Song 1058 speaks after such a word: it marvels at the word of grace that killed the five senses and turned death away (கருணை வார்த்தை இருந்தவாறு என்). The pair moves from asking for the guru's word to wondering at its effect.

Tirumanthiram 1823 maps the temple onto the person: the heart is the great temple, the body the shrine, the soul the linga (உள்ளம் பெருங்கோயில் ... சீவன் சிவலிங்கம்). The song takes the inward temple one step further: the temple is silence that no one can measure (அரிய மோனமே கோயில்), the flowers are the joy of knowledge, and the worship goes to a Siva-form beyond Vedas, words and action. Both move worship inside; the song places it beyond even the heart, in silence.

The song calls its inward worship in the temple of silence the great worship (மாபூசை புரிவேனே). Tirumanthiram 1852 gives the same name to worship in the place where sun and moon do not shine (இலங்காத் தலத்திடை வந்தித்தல் நந்திக்கு மாபூசை) and sends outer worship to the asuras. Both keep the word மாபூசை for worship beyond outward rite.

The song rejects the yogi who thinks the breath, if turned back (வாயு அடைய மீளில் வீடாகும் என நாடி), gives release but who has no grace (அருள் பெறா), and asks to melt into the feet. Tirumanthiram 1854 also turns breath and mind back at the root, then sets the body aside and enters the Pure One's grace (புனிதன் அருள்தனில் புக்கிருந்து) before its worship is complete. Both make grace, not breath alone, the step that finishes the practice.

The song lists the yogic steps: the breath held, the fire kindled at the root (மூல ... அனல் மூள), nectar drunk, and the climb that strikes Yama (எமனை மோதி). Tirumanthiram 345 tells of Siva at Kadavur turning the fire at the root opening upward (மூலத் துவாரத்து மூளும் ஒருவனை) and burning Death (காலனைக் காய்ந்து) in the yoga of fire. The song applies to the practitioner the Death-defeating yoga the Tirumanthiram finds in the Kadavur story.

In Kural 1133 the lover says he once had shame and manliness and now has the palmyra horse lovers ride (காமுற்றார் ஏறும் மடல்). The song says women's eyes make even sleepless gods and Vedic ascetics free of infatuation resolve to mount it (துறவரான பேர் யாரும் மடலேறத் துணியுமாறு). The Kural's private loss of shame becomes in the song a power that undoes renunciation, and the poet asks for a way out.

The song asks what Murugan's form is: the form with parts (சகளமோ), the bud of the six supports, the support-less, or the formless (நிராகார வடிவேயோ). Tirumanthiram 1763 answers that the supreme Siva takes form, formlessness and form-with-formlessness together (உருவும் அருவும் உருவோடு அருவும்) and stands as guru to souls. The Tirumanthiram's 'all three' answers the song's 'which one?'.

The song asks for grace to sing the feet with love before Death, sent by Yama with noose and trident (ஏமனால் ஏவி விடு காலன் கொடிய பாசம்), arrives. Tirumanthiram 176 says there is no fighting the life's departure, but if one thinks of the Lord (அண்ணலை எண்ணும்) Death's messengers will not even think of harming one. The Tirumanthiram supplies the promise behind the song's plea.

Tirumanthiram 2217 describes the teacher passing from turiya to turiya-atita (சென்று துரியாதீதத்தே) and there becoming the stainless Supreme, so the states beyond turiya lead to the goal. The song says the abode of supreme wisdom is not reached above turiya (துரிய மீது சாராது) and is followed by no one. The conflict holds if சாராது means that no state beyond turiya reaches it; if it means only that turiya itself falls short, the two agree.

The song calls Murugan one who cannot be touched or seen directly (தொட அடாது ... வடிவு காண வாராது), other than all and yet knowledge itself (வேறாகி அறிவாகி). Tirumanthiram 3035 says he is awareness and life and the senses (உணர்வும் அவனே) yet cannot be reached by thought (எண்ணலும் ஆகான்). Both hold together the Lord's being the knowing in us and his being beyond its reach.

This song says the Lord entered the body and taught 'you and I' (நீ நானும் என நேர்மை நூல் கூறி). Song 1038 names liberation 'I become you and you become I' (நானே நீயாய் நீயே நானாய்). The split of 1050 is uncertain, but read together the formula is the teaching given in 1050 and the state sought in 1038.

In 1042 the poet asks to hear the guru say 'do not play in the filth of desire and infatuation for women' (மானார் மோகத்துடன் ஆசை மாசூடு ஆடாது) and to turn within. In 1051, after describing lovemaking, he vows that even as infatuation grows he will not forget the feet (மால் கூரினும் உன் நீப சீர்பாதம் மறவேனே). On the reading that 1051 accepts infatuation alongside remembrance, the two songs disagree on whether devotion requires leaving desire.

source_issues: 1038: ஡ in the second line stands for ஊ (ஊசாடு ஊசல்).
1040: lines 11 and 12 are garbled (பர்ழு டேவா னூடே பர்ரு டேயூர்).
